subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

To get cold feet

options.text: To get frost bite in winter
To become afraid to do something
To dip one’s feet in cold water

solution:
The correct answer is: **To become afraid to do something**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom** 'To get cold feet'** is used for expressing when someone becomes nervous or frightened about it because he/she think it will fail.

 
 
• **Example -** *I was going to try bungee jumping, but I got cold feet__.*
 
 
 
• So, it is clear that the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom **'To get cold feet'** is 'To become afraid to do something.'

Hence, the correct answer is **option 3.**
